title: Bathtub Caulking: Remove Old Caulk and Recaulk with 100% Silicone

locations.name: Bathroom
locations.basis: Transcript explicit mention: 'this is the bathroom' and discussion of tub caulking.

summary: This This Old House segment demonstrates removing seven-year-old caulk around a bathtub and recaulk­ing with 100% silicone. The host walks through surface preparation, debris protection, and tool setup, then demonstrates removing old caulk, masking the edges with painter’s tape, cutting and loading the caulk, applying a clean bead with a caulking gun, smoothing the bead with a finger, and finally removing the tape while the bead is wet and allowing the caulk to cure. The video emphasizes silicone’s advantages for bathroom joints (adheres to non-porous surfaces, mold/mildew resistance, and flexibility to accommodate movement) and cautions on ventilation and cure times: do not expose the fresh bead to moisture for 24 hours and wait about 30 minutes before it can get wet.
topics: Properties of silicone caulk (mold/mildew resistance, flexibility)
Caulking gun operation and nozzle cutting
Breaking the caulk seal and priming the tube
Bead application technique (steady hand, level gun, steady speed)
Curing times for bathroom caulk (30 minutes to wet, 24 hours to full cure)

sections.title: Assessment of issue and recaulk plan
concepts: Decision to remove old caulk and recaulk
sections.description: Host identifies seven-year-old caulk around the tub, notes signs of moisture leakage, and outlines a plan to remove the existing caulk and recaulk with silicone.

sections.title: Surface protection and initial caulk removal
concepts: Initial caulk removal and debris cleanup
sections.description: Preparation for work includes laying a drop cloth to protect the tub and floor, protecting the wall from debris, and starting to scrape and remove the old caulk along the tub and wall.

sections.title: Surface cleaning and ventilation setup
sections.description: Wipe down the area with alcohol and ensure good ventilation before continuing with surface prep for a clean caulk job.

sections.title: Masking tape for bead guidance
sections.description: Apply painter’s tape to establish a clean gap and guide a straight caulk bead, keeping the tape a quarter inch from the wall.

sections.title: Caulk choice and silicone properties
sections.description: Introduce a 100% silicone caulk and explain why silicone is preferred for bathrooms due to strong adhesion to non-porous surfaces, mold/mildew resistance, and long-term flexibility.

sections.title: Caulking gun basics and nozzle prep
concepts: Nozzle tip preparation and foil seal
sections.description: Demonstrate basic caulking gun operation, including the built-in cutter on the handle and the need to break the foil seal at the nozzle before loading caulk.

sections.title: Loading, cutting end, and priming the seal
concepts: Cutting the end of the tube
Breaking the seal for proper flow
sections.description: Show how to load the tube, cut the nozzle end to an appropriate size, break the seal, and prepare the tube for application.

sections.title: Bead application technique
concepts: Gun level, steady squeeze, consistent speed
sections.description: Demonstrate applying a continuous bead along the joint, keeping the gun level and moving at a steady pace to produce a clean line.

sections.title: Bead smoothing and void filling
concepts: Smoothing the bead with a finger
sections.description: With the bead still wet, smooth and fill any voids in the corner by running a finger along the joint to achieve a uniform bead.

sections.title: Tape removal while bead is wet
concepts: Removing tape while the bead is wet
Avoiding tape pull on the bead
sections.description: Carefully remove the masking tape while the bead is still wet to prevent pulling or tearing the bead.

sections.title: Final bead check and cure guidance
sections.description: Observe the completed bead for neatness and consistency; note the start of curing guidance and moisture restrictions after application.

sections.title: Curing times and moisture guidelines
sections.description: Explain that the caulk should not be exposed to moisture for about 30 minutes and will take up to 24 hours to fully cure.

sections.title: Closing and channel CTA
concepts: Viewer call to action (subscribe and explore more videos)
sections.description: Wrap up the segment with thanks, encourage viewers to check other This Old House videos, and invite subscriptions.
